findings.description: jwt.decode only base64-decodes the token and does not verify the signature, so SECRET is never used. Any client can forge a token with an arbitrary sub. Also, a malformed token makes decode return null, so claims.sub throws a TypeError that is passed to next(err) as a 500 instead of a 401.
findings.scenario: Authorization: Bearer <unsigned token with {"sub":"<admin id>"}> authenticates as that user. A token like 'abc' gives claims === null and a 500.
findings.fix: const claims = jwt.verify(token, SECRET, { algorithms: ['HS256'] }); and return 401 when verify throws.

findings.description: Assignment (=) is used instead of comparison (===) in requireAdmin. The condition is always truthy and it overwrites req.user.role with 'admin', so every authenticated user passes and is escalated for the rest of the request (and persisted if the user object is later saved).
findings.scenario: Any regular user calling an admin route gets next() and their role is set to 'admin'.

findings.description: forEach with an async callback does not await the deletions. The response is sent before sessions are deleted, and any rejection from db.sessions.delete is an unhandled promise rejection (which can crash Node). The response reports 'revoked' even if deletions fail.
findings.scenario: db.sessions.delete throws for one session: process gets an unhandledRejection, client still sees {revoked: N} and sessions remain valid.

findings.description: revokeSessions acts on req.params.id with no check that the caller is that user or an admin; it is also not wrapped in try/catch, so a DB error becomes an unhandled rejection in Express 4. Combined with the broken requireAdmin, any user can revoke any user's sessions.
findings.scenario: Authenticated user A calls the route with another user's id and logs them out.
findings.fix: Check req.user.id === req.params.id or role === 'admin' (strict comparison) before proceeding, and wrap in try/catch calling next(err).

findings.description: Revocation is capped by a user-supplied limit (default 50), so a user with more sessions is only partially logged out while the response claims success. Negative or huge limits are also unchecked.
findings.scenario: User has 200 sessions; revoke with default limit leaves 150 active.
findings.fix: Delete all sessions for the user (e.g. db.sessions.deleteByUser(id)) or loop until none remain; clamp limit if kept.

findings.description: SECRET is exported from the module, widening exposure of the signing key to any importer (logging, serialization).
findings.scenario: Another module imports SECRET and logs or returns it.

findings.description: claims.sub is passed straight to the DB lookup without validating type or existence, and no token expiry/issuer checks exist beyond what verify would give.
findings.scenario: Token with sub as an object may cause unexpected query behavior in some db layers.
